text: GPS satellite clocks must be corrected relative to clocks on Earth's surface. What does general relativity identify as the dominant reason?
choices: Special-relativistic time dilation from the satellites' orbital speed makes their clocks run fast.
Clocks deeper in the gravitational well run faster, so the ground clocks gain time on the satellites.
The relativity of simultaneity makes it impossible ever to synchronize ground and satellite clocks.
Gravitational time dilation makes the higher-altitude satellite clocks run faster than ground clocks.
explanation: Gravitational time dilation makes clocks run faster where gravity is weaker; at altitude the GPS clocks gain about 45 microseconds per day, dominating the roughly 7 microseconds per day of special-relativistic slowing from orbital speed (net about 38 μs/day). Option 0 reverses the special-relativistic effect (speed slows clocks) and it is not the dominant term; option 1 reverses the direction of gravitational dilation; option 2 misdescribes the mechanism.
